newsitem.title: USA: US 30yr bond off one point, dlr drop fuels selling.
newsitem.headline: US 30yr bond off one point, dlr drop fuels selling.

text.p: The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury briefly fell to a full-point loss in mid-morning trade on Friday as a dollar slide fueled profit-taking.
The dollar fell against the mark as the currency market was said to be pricing in prospects for a Bundesbank switch to a variable repo rate next week from a fixed rate.

"The weakness in the currency market was transmitted to the bond market," said Alan Levenson, director of research at Aubrey G. Lanston & Co, a primary government securities dealer. Levenson said a Bundesbank switch to a variable repo rate would pave the way for higher German interest rates.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond briefly fell a full point to 96-24/32, before cutting its loss by a quarter point.
"I think the (slide) simply shows you how skittish sentiment is in our bond market," said Levenson.
(( -- Ellen Freilich, North American Treasury Desk, 212-859-1679))
